correctness.rationale: The proof determines every mutually maximally distant pair from the canonical nested neighborhoods, converts strong metric bases to minimum vertex covers of the resulting strong resolving graph, classifies its maximum independent sets by a unique cut index, and counts them. The K2 boundary is separated explicitly. A literal brute-force verifier independently checks distances, MMD pairs, strong resolution, optimum size, and basis count for all 255 positive canonical profiles through order 9.

value.rationale: Strong metric dimension is NP-hard in general and is structurally different from ordinary metric dimension. The result gives an exact strong resolving graph for an infinite nested-neighborhood class, a one-line invariant sdim=N-p-1, and a complete classification and count of every minimum basis. It also separates what the invariant forgets (all class sizes except through N and p) from what the basis count retains, providing a natural structural refinement beyond a scalar computation.
